The invention provides a sealing material sheet for solar cell modules, as well as a sealing material-integrated rear-surface protecting sheet that includes the sealing material sheet.

The sealing material sheet has a total thickness in the range of 200 μm to 400 μm and is formed as a multilayer structure including at least a core layer and a skin layer. By adopting this layered configuration, the sheet can provide suitable sealing performance for a solar cell module while maintaining appropriate mechanical strength and processability.

The core layer contains resin components including polypropylene and low-density polyethylene. Based on the total mass of all resin components in the core layer, the polypropylene content is from 5% to 40% by mass, and the low-density polyethylene content is from 60% to 95% by mass. The low-density polyethylene contained in the core layer has a density of 0.910 g/cm³ to 0.940 g/cm³. This composition allows the core layer to contribute to the overall strength, heat resistance, and dimensional stability of the sealing material sheet.

The skin layer contains low-density polyethylene as its main resin component. Specifically, the skin layer contains 80% to 100% by mass of low-density polyethylene having a density of at least 0.880 g/cm³ and less than 0.910 g/cm³. The skin layer contains no polypropylene. Because the skin layer is formed from low-density polyethylene having this relatively low density, it can provide favorable adhesion, flexibility, and sealing properties at the surface of the sheet.

Through the combination of the core layer and the skin layer having the above-described resin compositions and density ranges, the sealing material sheet is suitable for use in solar cell modules. In particular, it can be integrated with a rear-surface protecting sheet to form a sealing material-integrated rear-surface protecting sheet, thereby improving handling and simplifying the production of solar cell modules.
outputs.L4:
A sealing material sheet for solar cell modules and an integrated rear-surface protecting sheet are provided. The sealing material sheet is designed for use in the encapsulation and protection of photovoltaic elements in a solar cell module, and is particularly suitable for arrangement on the rear-surface side of the module. The sheet has a multilayer structure with a total thickness of 200 μm to 400 μm, thereby providing sufficient mechanical strength, handling properties, and protective performance while maintaining flexibility and processability during module lamination.

The multilayer structure includes a core layer and at least one skin layer. The core layer contains a resin composition including polypropylene and low-density polyethylene. By combining polypropylene with low-density polyethylene in the core layer, the sheet can obtain an improved balance of heat resistance, dimensional stability, flexibility, and adhesion-related performance. The polypropylene contributes rigidity and thermal stability, while the low-density polyethylene contributes softness, melt flow characteristics, and compatibility with encapsulating processes used in solar cell module manufacture.

The skin layer is formed from a resin composition that is substantially free of polypropylene and contains low-density polyethylene as a principal component. Because the skin layer does not contain polypropylene, it can exhibit improved compatibility with adjacent encapsulating materials and module components, particularly where polyethylene-based or olefin-based sealing materials are used. The low-density polyethylene skin layer also promotes favorable surface properties, including improved conformity to uneven surfaces, reduced risk of interfacial defects, and enhanced sealing performance during heat and pressure lamination.

The low-density polyethylene used in the skin layer preferably has a density within a specified range suitable for solar cell module sealing applications. By selecting the density of the low-density polyethylene within this range, the sheet can maintain appropriate flexibility, adhesion, melt behavior, and long-term durability. Similarly, the resin composition of the core layer is selected so that the combined polypropylene and low-density polyethylene provide the desired mechanical and thermal properties without impairing the sealing function of the sheet.

The resulting sealing material sheet can be used as part of an integrated rear-surface protecting sheet for a solar cell module. In such an integrated sheet, the sealing function and the rear-surface protection function are combined, reducing the number of separate layers required in module assembly. This integration can simplify the manufacturing process, improve layer-to-layer compatibility, and reduce the possibility of delamination or defects caused by poor adhesion between dissimilar materials.

When incorporated into a solar cell module, the sheet protects the solar cell elements from moisture, mechanical stress, and environmental degradation. The multilayer configuration allows the sheet to provide both internal strength and surface compatibility. The polypropylene/low-density polyethylene core layer supports dimensional stability and durability, while the polypropylene-free low-density polyethylene skin layer improves contact and sealing with adjacent module layers.

Accordingly, the described sealing material sheet and integrated rear-surface protecting sheet provide a practical material configuration for solar cell module encapsulation. The specified layer thickness, multilayer construction, resin compositions, and density ranges contribute to improved module protection, enhanced compatibility with encapsulating materials, stable lamination performance, and long-term reliability of the solar cell module.

“Provided” is a simple word, but it plays an important role in communication. It often introduces a condition, meaning that something will happen only if a certain requirement is met. For example, “You can join the event, provided you register in advance” means that registration is necessary.

The word is useful in formal writing, agreements, instructions, and everyday conversations. It helps make expectations clear and prevents misunderstandings. By using “provided,” speakers and writers can explain rules, limits, or possibilities in a precise way.

In a broader sense, “provided” can also suggest support or supply. When someone says that resources were provided, it means that the necessary materials, help, or information were made available. Whether used to express a condition or to describe something given, “provided” is a practical and meaningful word in English.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a technical summary in the style of a patent publication for an invention involving a sealing material sheet for photovoltaic modules and a rear-surface protecting sheet integrated with the sealing material.
counterfactuals.output:
## Technical Summary

Disclosed is a sealing material sheet for a photovoltaic module and a rear-surface protecting sheet integrated with the sealing material, suitable for use in the manufacture of crystalline silicon, thin-film, and other photovoltaic modules. The sheet is configured to improve module reliability, simplify lamination processing, and enhance resistance to moisture ingress, heat, ultraviolet radiation, and electrical degradation.

The sealing material sheet comprises a thermoplastic or thermosetting resin composition having transparency, adhesion, and encapsulating properties required for sealing photovoltaic elements. In one embodiment, the sealing material includes an ethylene-based copolymer resin, such as ethylene-vinyl acetate, ethylene-α-olefin copolymer, ionomer resin, or a polyolefin-based elastomer. The resin composition may further include one or more additives selected from a crosslinking agent, silane coupling agent, antioxidant, ultraviolet absorber, light stabilizer, heat stabilizer, acid acceptor, and adhesion promoter. The composition is formed into a sheet having a thickness suitable for encapsulating solar cells and electrically conductive interconnectors.

The rear-surface protecting sheet integrated with the sealing material includes a rear protective layer and a sealing material layer laminated or coextruded thereon. The rear protective layer may comprise a weather-resistant resin film, fluororesin film, polyester film, polyamide film, polyolefin film, inorganic vapor-deposited film, metal foil, or a multilayer laminate thereof. The sealing material layer is provided on a surface of the rear protective layer facing the photovoltaic elements during module assembly. By integrating the sealing material with the rear-surface protecting sheet in advance, the number of components handled during module production can be reduced, thereby improving positional accuracy, suppressing wrinkles and entrapped air, and shortening assembly time.

In certain embodiments, the integrated sheet includes an adhesive or tie layer between the rear protective layer and the sealing material layer. The tie layer may include a modified polyolefin, urethane adhesive, acrylic adhesive, epoxy adhesive, or silane-containing resin composition to improve interlayer adhesion before and after lamination. The rear protective layer may further include a barrier layer for suppressing water vapor transmission, a reflective layer for improving light utilization, an insulating layer for maintaining dielectric strength, and/or a surface-treated layer for enhancing adhesion to the sealing material.

The sealing material layer may be designed to exhibit a controlled melt viscosity during vacuum lamination so as to fill gaps around photovoltaic cells and wiring members while preventing excessive resin flow beyond module edges. The layer may also be formulated to suppress generation of acetic acid, bubbles, voids, discoloration, and delamination under high-temperature and high-humidity conditions. Where a crosslinkable composition is used, the degree of crosslinking after lamination may be adjusted to provide heat resistance and creep resistance while maintaining sufficient flexibility to accommodate thermal expansion differences among module components.

A photovoltaic module according to the disclosure may include, in order from a light-receiving side, a front transparent protective member, a front sealing material layer, photovoltaic elements, and the integrated rear-surface protecting sheet having the sealing material layer facing the photovoltaic elements. During lamination, the sealing material layer of the integrated rear sheet bonds to the photovoltaic elements and associated conductive members, while the rear protective layer forms the external rear surface of the module.

The integrated construction provides one or more of the following technical effects: improved moisture resistance; enhanced adhesion between the encapsulant and backsheet; improved electrical insulation; reduced risk of backsheet delamination; reduced module manufacturing steps; improved handling of thin sealing layers; improved appearance by reducing wrinkles, bubbles, and misalignment; and enhanced long-term durability under outdoor exposure.

The invention is applicable to photovoltaic modules requiring high reliability over extended service periods, including building-mounted, utility-scale, vehicle-mounted, and flexible photovoltaic modules.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
